questions: Does the fusion gain over Moonstone alone persist inside latitude bands, or is it carried by one region?
If the two feature blocks are given learnable scalar weights instead of a fixed 1.0, what weights does the model choose and does that beat plain concatenation?

bands.equatorial: center latitude 9 to 30 degrees (355 Val rows)
bands.mid: center latitude 30 to 60 degrees (450 Val rows)
bands.polar: center latitude 60 to 90 degrees (350 Val rows)

cells.stratified: features (moonstone_256, fusion_1024) x heads (linear, linear_balanced) x 3 seeds
cells.gated: learnable scalar gate w1 for the Moonstone block and w2 for the NASA block, initialised at 1.0, then the same linear heads, 3 seeds

metric: macro-F1 over the full 49 classes computed inside each latitude band, plus the overall value as a consistency check
acceptance: Latitude comes only from the authenticated metadata export keyed by patch id
Overall per-cell values must reproduce the earlier fusion matrix
No Test ID is read or scored
claims_not_permitted: Regional or geological interpretation of the band differences
Statistical significance: bands hold 350-450 Val rows and three seeds
